newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RYAN SMYTH GETS HAT TRICK AS OILERS BEAT LEAFS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RYAN SMYTH GETS HAT TRICK AS OILERS BEAT LEAFS.

text.p: Ryan Smyth recorded his first career hat trick, including the tie-breaking goal with 2:14 remaining, to lift the Edmonton Oilers to their third straight win, 4-2 over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday.
"This is big time, scoring three gaols in the NHL," Smyth said. "It's a great feeling."
Smyth, who had two goals in 48 games last season, scored his second of the game and third of the season to snap a 2-2 tie and lead the Oilers to a league-high six points.

After a turnover at centre ice, Smyth broke down the right side with Doug Weight on the left. Weight's cross-ice pass was tipped by Toronto defenceman Dimitri Yushkevich, but Smyth grabbed the loose puck and beat goaltender Felix Potvin to the right side of the net.
Smyth's empty-net goal with eight seconds remaining closed the scoring.
The Oilers have opened with three straight wins for the first time since 1985. Curtis Joseph has allowed just five goals on 83 shots this season.
Potvin made 33 saves for Toronto, which has split its first two contests.
"We had a good game, I thought we didn't come out the way we should've but we showed a lot to come back," Toronto's Mats Sundin said. "We made some mistakes and that cost us."
Jason Arnott had the other Edmonton tally while Mike Craig and Sundin tallied for Toronto.
Doug Gilmour assisted on Sundin's goal for his 1,042nd point, moving him past Joe Mullen into 38th place on the all-time list.
Edmonton played without enforcer Louie DeBrusk, who was suspended one game pending an NHL hearing after he received a match penalty Sunday for slashing Vancouver's Dana Murzyn.

At Florida, Adam Graves scored off a goalmouth scramble with 32 seconds left in regulation, lifting the winless New York Rangers into a 1-1 tie with the Panthers in the finale of a home-and-home series.
Graves put a backhander over the left shoulder of goaltender John Vanbiesbrouck, who had made a series of stops moments earlier.
"It was a bouncing puck on end and that made it easier for me to get my stick on it," Graves said.
The play started after the Rangers pulled goalie Glenn Healy for an extra attacker and won a faceoff deep in the Panthers' zone following a controversial icing call.
The Rangers (0-1-2) are off to their worst start since opening the 1986-87 season 0-3-1.
New York played without captain Mark Messier, who served the first game of his two-game suspension for slamming Florida left wing Mike Hough into the boards from behind on Sunday.
The Panthers raised their Eastern Conference championship banner during pre-game ceremonies.

At Colorado, Patrick Roy stopped 24 shots for his 31st career shutout and five different players scored first-period goals as the NHL champion Avalanche got their first win of the season, a 6-0 rout of the San Jose Sharks.
Roy made six saves in the first period, 11 in the second and seven in the third for his second shutout with Colorado.
The Avalanche, who raised their Stanley Cup championship banner in pre-game ceremonies, opened the season with losses at St. Louis and Dallas. The Sharks fell to 1-1-1.
Jon Klemm, Rene Corbet, Eric Lacroix, Uwe Krupp and Sandis Ozolinsh all scored in the first period for Colorado while Peter Forsberg added a third-period goal.
In Dallas, Mike Modano scored his first two goals of the season and added two assists as the Stars defeated the Washington Capitals 5-3.
Jere Lehtinen, Jamie Langenbrunner and Greg Adams scored the other goals for Dallas while Keith Jones, Phil Housley and Jason Allison tallied for Washington.

Andy Moog made 23 saves for Dallas (2-0) while Jim Carey stopped 22 shots for Washington (0-2). Carey, who won the Vezina Trophy last season before struggling in the playoffs, has allowed 10 goals in two games.
Dallas played without centre Joe Nieuwendyk, who suffered a chest contusion when checked by Colorado's Peter Forsberg in Saturday's season opener.
In Hartford, Geoff Sanderson scored two goals and set up another and Jeff O'Neill tallied twice, leading the Whalers to a 7-3 victory over the Pittsburgh Penguins.
Brian Glynn, Kevin Dineen and Brendan Shanahan also scored and Andrei Nikolishin picked up three assists for the Whalers, who are off to their second 2-0 start in as many seasons.
Mario Lemieux had a goal and an assist for Pittsburgh (0-2).
